task: Fix a parser bug where unary minus is tokenized as a binary operator after a left parenthesis.

candidate_memories.content: Recent failing test: parse('(-1)') emits unexpected BinaryExpr node.
Last attempted fix in lexer.go only changed whitespace handling and did not affect minus token classification.
Parser precedence rules treat unary operators in parsePrefix, not in parseInfix.
AST changed last week: PrefixExpr replaced UnaryExpr.
Legacy note: minus after left parenthesis is always binary and should be handled in parseInfix.
When parsers fail around unary operators, preserve failing input examples and inspect prefix vs infix dispatch.
